copy.blurb:
A +6.8pp gap on the the draw side. Germany v Curaçao in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has the draw stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

On Elo, Germany comes in 420 points ahead — Germany at 1900, Curaçao at 1480. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Germany to win at 83%, the draw at 10%, and Curaçao to win at 7%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. the draw sits at 10% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Germany to win at 94%, the draw at 3%, and Curaçao to win at 3%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the the draw side — 3% on the market, 10% on the engine, a +6.8pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the the draw side that lower bound is 10% — +6.8pp clear of the market's 3%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the the draw side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 23 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read. Per BBC Sport (football): "Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with…" The Guardian (football) carried the same line: "Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]"
